subject: chemistry
title: Radical Realm: Free Radical Chains
welcome_lead: Follow the initiation, propagation and termination of radical chains.
meta_desc: A-Level chemistry adventure on free radical substitution.
final_note: You traced unpaired electrons through every chain step.

concepts.def: Radical reacts to form new radical.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Initiation: Cl2 -> 2Cl. (UV light, homolytic).

Propagation: Cl. + CH4 -> CH3. + HCl; CH3. + Cl2 -> CH3Cl + Cl.

Two radicals combine: Cl. + Cl. -> Cl2; Cl. + CH3. -> CH3Cl; CH3. + CH3. -> C2H6.

These remove radicals from the system but happen rarely compared to propagation.

Further substitution: CH3Cl can react again -> CH2Cl2, CHCl3, CCl4. Mixture of products.

Excess CH4 reduces over-chlorination. Industrially used for production of chloromethanes; not a clean synthesis of one product.

options: A catalyst lowers the activation energy of the original reaction pathway.

mcqs.q: Can you determine the order of a reaction with respect to a reactant from the balanced equation?
options: A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.
The order of reaction is always equal to the number of reactants in the equation.
No — orders must be determined experimentally; they often differ from the stoichiometric coefficients.
The order of reaction with respect to each reactant equals its coefficient in the balanced equation.
